**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2025. Time allowed: three hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklets are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (One Hour): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (30 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (1 hour): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Distinguish between

(i) FM and AM radio transmission *[2 marks]*

(ii) a radio transmitter and receiver *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) In **AM (amplitude modulation)** the amplitude of the high-frequency carrier wave is varied in step with the audio signal, while the carrier frequency stays constant. In **FM (frequency modulation)** the frequency of the carrier is varied in step with the audio signal (the shift is proportional to the signal amplitude), while the carrier amplitude stays constant.
Consequences: FM is much less affected by noise and interference (which mostly change the amplitude) and gives better sound quality, but needs a wider bandwidth and has a shorter range; AM is simpler and has a longer range but is more noisy.

(ii) A **radio transmitter** produces the radio-frequency carrier (oscillator), mixes it with the audio signal from the microphone (modulator), amplifies the modulated signal (power amplifier) and sends it into space through an aerial.
A **radio receiver** picks the radio waves up with its aerial, selects the wanted station (tuner), separates the audio signal from the carrier (demodulator or detector), amplifies it (audio amplifier) and converts it back into sound (loudspeaker).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) List two sources of power loses in optical fibres. *[2 marks]*

(ii) The speed of light in the core of an optical fibre is $1.97\times10^{8}\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and the critical angle of incidence at the core-cladding boundary is $76.4^\circ$. Calculate the refractive index of the cladding material. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Two sources of power loss (attenuation) in an optical fibre (any two):

1. **Absorption** of light by impurities (for example metal ions and water) and by the glass itself, which turns light energy into heat.
2. **Scattering** of light by tiny density variations and imperfections in the glass (Rayleigh scattering), so that some light leaves the guided path.
3. (Also acceptable: **bending losses** at sharp bends, where the angle of incidence falls below the critical angle; **loss at joints and connectors**, from misalignment or reflection at the ends.)

(ii) Take $c = 3.00\times10^{8}\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ (not printed in the paper). Refractive index of the core:
$$n_{\mathrm{core}} = \frac{c}{v} = \frac{3.00\times10^{8}}{1.97\times10^{8}} = 1.523.$$

At the critical angle $C$ the refracted ray grazes the boundary (angle of refraction $90^\circ$), so $n_{\mathrm{core}}\sin C = n_{\mathrm{clad}}\sin 90^\circ$:
$$n_{\mathrm{clad}} = n_{\mathrm{core}}\sin C = 1.523\times\sin 76.4^\circ = 1.523\times0.9720 = 1.48.$$

**Refractive index of the cladding $\approx 1.48$** (less than the core index of $1.52$, as required for total internal reflection).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Draw a block diagram of a radio receiver *[4 marks]*

(ii) State one advantage and one disadvantage of WhatsApp over SMS as communication channels. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Block diagram (to be drawn by the candidate), signal flowing from left to right:**

$$\boxed{\text{Aerial}} \longrightarrow \boxed{\text{Tuner (RF amplifier)}} \longrightarrow \boxed{\text{Demodulator (detector)}} \longrightarrow \boxed{\text{Audio amplifier}} \longrightarrow \boxed{\text{Loudspeaker}}$$

The **aerial** picks up many radio signals; the **tuner** (a tuned circuit, with a radio-frequency amplifier) selects the wanted carrier frequency; the **demodulator** removes the carrier and recovers the audio signal; the **audio amplifier** increases its power; the **loudspeaker** converts it to sound. (A superheterodyne receiver adds a mixer with a local oscillator and an intermediate-frequency amplifier between the tuner and the demodulator.)

(ii) **Advantage of WhatsApp:** it uses an internet data connection, so messages cost very little (or nothing over Wi-Fi), and it can send photos, voice notes, video, documents, locations and group messages, with delivery and read receipts.
**Disadvantage of WhatsApp:** it needs a smartphone and an internet connection (data or Wi-Fi), so it fails where there is no internet coverage or no data bundle; an SMS needs only a basic phone and the mobile network signal.
